Schizotypal personality disorder is characterized by cognitive and perceptual distortions such as magical thinking, unusual perceptual experiences, odd thinking and speech, and marked eccentricity or oddness [Psichiatry_DSM-5_3110][Psichiatry_DSM-5_3141]. In contrast, paranoid personality disorder is defined by a pervasive pattern of distrust and suspiciousness in which others’ motives are interpreted as malevolent, without the accompanying cognitive/perceptual distortions [Psichiatry_DSM-5_3097][Psichiatry_DSM-5_3074].
